claims.claim: Victorian coroner David Ryan found Richard Norton, 75, suffered a cardiac arrest after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC-1295 and ipamorelin.
claims.episode_span: Richard Norton, 75, an Australian actor, stuntman and fight choreographer, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC-1295 and ipamorelin.
claims.source_title: Coroner calls for TGA to review unapproved peptides after death of Australian actor
claims.supporting_quote: Victorian coroner David Ryan found Norton suffered a cardiac arrest after injecting the unapproved products CJC1295 and ipamorelin, which had been prescribed to him by a doctor.

claims.claim: The coroner recommended the TGA consider shifting the peptides from schedule 4 to schedule 10, limited to clinical trials or other experimental use.
claims.episode_span: Ryan recommended the TGA review benefits and safety and consider moving the peptides from Schedule 4, prescription-only, to Schedule 10, limited to clinical trials or other experimental use
claims.source_title: Coroner calls for TGA to review unapproved peptides after death of Australian actor
claims.supporting_quote: That review should consider shifting peptides from schedule 4 prescription-only drugs to schedule 10, allowing them only for clinical trials or other experimental use.

claims.claim: HHS announced plans to allow compounding pharmacies to prepare six peptides not approved by the FDA, including BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and Epitalon.
claims.episode_span: Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. released plans, announced in the Federal Register, to let compounding pharmacies prepare six peptides the FDA has not approved: BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and Epitalon.
claims.source_title: HIMS Stock Jumps 5% After HHS Temporarily Clears Compounding Of Six Peptides
claims.supporting_quote: HHS said it will not go after state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities, or licensed doctors for compounding six peptides—BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500.

claims.claim: The peptide-access draft came from the health secretary's office rather than the FDA, and a two-week public comment period follows official publication.
claims.episode_span: The draft came from the health secretary's office rather than the FDA. After official publication, a two-week public comment period follows.
claims.source_title: US Health Secretary RFK Jr to expand access to unapproved peptides
claims.supporting_quote: In an unusual move, the draft came from the office of the health secretary rather than the FDA. After the plan has been officially published later this week, there will be a two-week public comment period.

claims.claim: An FDA advisory panel voted in July to loosen restrictions on the six peptides, but FDA staff recommended against it.
claims.episode_span: An FDA advisory panel voted in July to loosen restrictions; FDA staff recommended against that step.
claims.source_title: US Health Secretary RFK Jr to expand access to unapproved peptides
claims.supporting_quote: An FDA advisory panel voted in July to loosen restrictions on the six peptides. But FDA staff members recommended against it.

claims.claim: Partnership for Safe Medicines said the enforcement-discretion decision leaves Americans in a grey area and that many newly appointed PCAC members appear to have conflicts of interest.
claims.episode_span: The Partnership for Safe Medicines said the decision leaves a grey area, that FDA scientists had recommended against the substances over evidence concerns, and that many newly appointed Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee members appear to have conflicts of interest.
claims.source_title: Statement on the FDA and HHS enforcement discretion policy for 503a compounding with certain peptides
claims.supporting_quote: Today's decision leaves Americans in a grey area as to whether peptides are safe or not, even though the FDA’s own scientists recommended against voting in favor of these substances due to concerns with evidence.

claims.claim: Eli Lilly said investigational retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Ozempic in a large diabetes study.
claims.episode_span: Eli Lilly said its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk's Ozempic in a large diabetes study.
claims.source_title: STAT+: Lilly’s triple-G drug beats Ozempic in head-to-head study
claims.supporting_quote: Eli Lilly announced that its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic in a large diabetes study.

claims.claim: Ascletis reported a placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction of 1.7% at 12 weeks for oral small-molecule GLP-1 ASC30 in a U.S. phase II study in participants with diabetes.
claims.episode_span: Ascletis reported that ASC30, an investigational oral small-molecule GLP-1 rather than a peptide, produced a placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction of 1.7 percent at 12 weeks in a U.S. phase II study in participants with diabetes.
claims.source_title: Ascletis' Oral Small Molecule GLP-1, ASC30, Demonstrated Placebo-Adjusted HbA1c Reduction of 1.7% at 12 Weeks from Its U.S. Phase II Study in Participants with Diabetes
claims.supporting_quote: Ascletis' Oral Small Molecule GLP-1, ASC30, Demonstrated Placebo-Adjusted HbA1c Reduction of 1.7% at 12 Weeks from Its U.S. Phase II Study in Participants with Diabetes

claims.claim: A survey identified 33 unique compounded semaglutide and/or tirzepatide products, two-thirds semaglutide and one-third tirzepatide, with 48 percent containing added ingredients.
claims.episode_span: Two-thirds of the 33 products contained semaglutide and one-third contained tirzepatide. Forty-eight percent combined semaglutide or tirzepatide with some mix of cyanocobalamin, glycine, niacinamide, docusate or ondansetron.
claims.source_title: Compounded Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Products Use Unique Formulations but Efficacy and Safety Largely Unknown
claims.supporting_quote: We identified 33 unique semaglutide and/or tirzepatide products. Two-thirds contained semaglutide, and one-third contained tirzepatide. Forty-eight percent of products contained either semaglutide or tirzepatide with some combination of cyanocobalamin, glycine, niacinamide, docusate, or ondansetron.

claims.claim: Testing identified a widespread previously unidentified impurity in compounded tirzepatide-B12 products from a chemical reaction between tirzepatide and certain B12 analogs.
claims.episode_span: Expert Opinion on Drug Safety reports a widespread, previously unidentified impurity formed by a chemical reaction between tirzepatide and certain B12 analogs, present at substantial levels.
claims.source_title: A novel, widespread impurity in mass-compounded tirzepatide/B12 products: potential patient safety implications
claims.supporting_quote: Our testing identified a widespread and previously unidentified impurity in compounded tirzepatide-B12 products resulting from a chemical reaction between tirzepatide and certain analogs of B12.

claims.claim: In a retrospective study of 94 people, average weight loss at 3 months on compounded semaglutide/cyanocobalamin was 4.11 kg or 4.57 percent.
claims.episode_span: After three months, average weight loss was 4.11 kilograms, or 4.57 percent.
claims.source_title: Weight loss and body composition after compounded semaglutide treatment in a real world setting
claims.supporting_quote: After 3 months, average weight loss was 4.11 (2.77) kg or 4.57% (2.96%).

claims.claim: Three poison-center cases involved incorrect administration of compounded semaglutide, including two tenfold dosing errors with nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain.
claims.episode_span: The Journal of the American Pharmacists Association described three adverse-event reports to a regional poison control center after incorrect administration of semaglutide obtained for weight loss from compounding pharmacies and an aesthetic spa.
claims.source_title: Administration errors of compounded semaglutide reported to a poison control center-Case series
claims.supporting_quote: We report 3 cases of adverse drug events after incorrect administration of semaglutide for weight loss obtained from compounding pharmacies and an aesthetic spa. Two patients self-administered 10-fold dosing errors.

claims.claim: Semaglutide is FDA approved as Ozempic for type 2 diabetes and Wegovy for overweight or obesity.
claims.episode_span: Semaglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist: a peptide that acts at the GLP-1 receptor and, in its approved forms, is used to lower blood sugar and, at the Wegovy brand, to treat overweight or obesity.
claims.source_title: Navigating compounded semaglutide: what health care providers need to know
claims.supporting_quote: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, is FDA approved under the brand names Ozempic for treatment of type 2 diabetes and Wegovy for the treatment of overweight or obesity.
